core.title: Name DESIRED OUTCOME files {STEP_CODE}{NNN}, with no prefix
core.given: A DESIRED OUTCOME file exists or is being created, renamed, moved, or reviewed.
core.when: You choose, change, or check its file name.
core.then: Ensure the file name matches the plan-artifact name pattern from the profile: the step code followed by the sequence number, with no prefix.
prefer: Step-coded names: the step code followed by the sequence number, in the profile's plan-artifact name pattern.
When you find an existing DESIRED OUTCOME file with a non-conforming name, rename it to the conforming pattern.
avoid: Any prefix before the step code (for example an artifact-kind or owning-unit prefix) — the name must be step-coded with no prefix.
core.why: The filename is the DESIRED OUTCOME URN's step-coded sequence segment, so a predictable {STEP_CODE}{NNN} name keeps file and URN aligned.
evidence: Every DESIRED OUTCOME file name matches the plan-artifact name pattern from the profile (step code then sequence number) with no prefix.
verification: DESIRED OUTCOME files are identified by artifact kind, location in the plan tree, or content shape, as the profile's role-assignment policy specifies; the filename check runs over that set.

A filename check pattern-matches every DESIRED OUTCOME file present against the plan-artifact name pattern from the profile; it applies to all DESIRED OUTCOME files present, not only those changed in the diff.
STEP_CODE comes from the step-code vocabulary defined by the companion convention; the sequence number is serialized as that pattern prescribes. No prefix before the step code is allowed.
Detecting already-present, misnamed DESIRED OUTCOME files that the current task did not touch needs a new observer: the repository-wide filename check above reporting a filename-mismatch finding.
No exceptions: the rule's unless is empty, so the check has no carve-outs. Detector, validator and finding ids are realization details; the core describes the check generically.

fires: A new DESIRED OUTCOME file is created for a product capability.
An existing DESIRED OUTCOME file is renamed.
A DESIRED OUTCOME file is moved to another location in the plan tree.
A plan is reviewed or validated and an existing DESIRED OUTCOME file is encountered whose name does not match the conforming pattern (e.g. carries a prefix), and must be corrected.
A task touches DESIRED OUTCOME files without mentioning the term 'DESIRED OUTCOME' (e.g. 'add the next step for this product capability').
doesNotFire: Editing the contents of an already correctly named DESIRED OUTCOME file without changing its name.
Naming acceptance, product capability, or other non-desired-outcome plan files.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete file-name pattern (including its suffix) that a plan artifact must match; instantiates the core's 'step code + sequence number, no prefix' obligation into the stack's exact serialization.
The concrete artifact kind that plays the plan-step role in this stack, so any file recognized as that kind is in scope whatever operation touches it.
How a file in this stack is recognized as a plan-step (DESIRED OUTCOME) artifact and assigned to the plan-artifact role, so the filename check scopes to exactly that set of files.
profileRequirements.bunValue: by its artifact kind / location in the plan tree or by desired-outcome-shaped YAML content

bunOnly.text: values: ["desired-outcome-filename-mismatch"] — the finding id of this rule's check.
bunOnly.reason: Finding ids of a single rule are realization details (notProfileKeys); the core keeps the fact but names the check generically as a desired outcome filename-mismatch finding over all existing DESIRED OUTCOME files (needs_new_observer).

bunOnly.text: Term 'filename' = the DESIRED OUTCOME file name; values.pattern = '{STEP_CODE}{NNN}.yaml'. STEP_CODE comes from the step-code vocabulary (planner.desired-outcome.step-code-vocabulary); NNN is the sequence number, shown as three digits in all source examples (E001, L045, K023).
bunOnly.reason: The term/pattern notation, the concrete serialization (with the .yaml suffix and the three-digit NNN padding read off the examples) and the companion-rule id reference are ATDD-Bun realization details; the neutral core takes the pattern from suffix.plan_artifact and the step-code source from the companion step-code convention.

bunOnly.text: Step-coded names such as E001.yaml, L045.yaml, K023.yaml.
bunOnly.reason: Concrete realization examples carrying the stack's file suffix; bun.json itself is delivered as the reference example, so the core states the shape at role level.

bunOnly.text: Every DESIRED OUTCOME file name matches {STEP_CODE}{NNN}.yaml (e.g. E001.yaml, L045.yaml, K023.yaml) with no prefix.
bunOnly.reason: Same concrete pattern and examples as prefer[0]; the core's evidence cites the profile's plan-artifact name pattern instead.

The neutral shape — step code then sequence number, no prefix — is the core obligation; the concrete '{STEP_CODE}{NNN}.yaml' (its .yaml suffix and padding) comes from the profile. bun.json's unless is empty, so the core adds no exceptions.
Neutral and kept entirely in the core: the filename/URN alignment rationale is rule content. bun.json states no concrete DESIRED OUTCOME URN shape, so no urn.* profile key is required for this rule.
Core keeps the role-level shape (step code + sequence number per the plan-artifact name pattern); the concrete E001.yaml-style examples stay in the Bun reference.
Neutral: rename non-conforming existing DESIRED OUTCOME files to the conforming pattern; no obligation added or dropped.

The no-prefix prohibition is neutral; the literal illustration prefixes ('desired-outcome-', wagon-name) are generalized to artifact-kind/owning-unit prefixes, the literals remain in the Bun reference.
Core states the evidence against the profile pattern; the concrete pattern and examples stay in the Bun reference.

Generic scope and enforcement — all DESIRED OUTCOME files present not just the diff, no prefix, step code from the companion vocabulary — map to core:verification; the concrete pattern serialization comes from the profile; term ids, the three-digit note and the planner.desired-outcome.step-code-vocabulary id reference are bunOnly.

The file_kind value 'desired outcome' is a methodology artifact kind (closed vocabulary), kept in the core; the concrete artifact kind name comes from roles.plan_artifact.kinds, and how a stack recognizes such files (artifact kind, plan-tree location, content shape) is role-assignment policy from roles.assignment. The fact's explanatory note is folded into core:verification.
Operations are already neutral; kept verbatim. The note's coverage explanation is reflected in the core's fires.

The fact itself (a needs_new_observer filename-mismatch finding activates the rule for already-present files) is core; the finding id string 'desired-outcome-filename-mismatch' is a realization detail.

neutralityNotes: DESIRED OUTCOME, product capability, step code, sequence number, plan tree and URN are ATDD methodology concepts (they appear in the closed vocabulary's params and examples), not stack mechanics, so they stay in the core. The only genuinely stack-specific content is the concrete file-name serialization — the .yaml suffix, the three-digit NNN padding and the term/pattern notation — supplied to the core through suffix.plan_artifact, plus this rule's finding id and the companion-rule id reference, which remain in the Bun realization (bunOnly). How a file is recognized as a DESIRED OUTCOME artifact (kind, plan-tree location, desired-outcome-shaped YAML content) is stack data carried by roles.assignment, not a path pattern; bun.json supplies no concrete plan-item path pattern, so layout.plan_item is not required. The filename/URN alignment rationale lives in core.why; bun.json states no concrete DESIRED OUTCOME URN shape, so no urn.* key is required. bun.json's unless is empty and the core keeps it empty: no exception was dropped or added. No profile keys were missing, so proposedKeys is empty.
